title: Called-zone contours by regime
caption: Contours where the called-strike probability is 50% for a 72-inch batter, standardised to the 2024 pitch mix, in 2024 (pre-buffer), 2025 (buffer cut) and 2026 (ABS challenge). Shading is the pointwise 95% interval of the contour along 120 rays from the zone centre, from 1,000 coefficient draws. The grey rectangle is the ABS zone, 17 in wide and 27% to 53.5% of height; the dotted line is where the ball touches it, 1.45 in outside. The lower panels enlarge the top, bottom and side edges and do not keep the aspect ratio. Top-edge caveat (annex 8.7, D-R0-04): every top-edge interval here is read as slightly too narrow. In the synthetic recovery the top edge's 95% interval covered the truth in 91 of 100 replicates, against a bound of 93. Its null 90% interval lay within 0.10 in of zero for 44 of 50, against 47, so a top-edge equivalence reading is underpowered. Half-width shortfall (annex 8.7): its null 90% interval covered zero in 42 of 50 replicates, against a bound of 43.
alt: Three nested closed curves over a strike-zone rectangle, lightest for 2024 and darkest for 2026. The 2026 curve's top edge sits at 40.7 in against 41.2 in for 2024, and its bottom edge at 17.7 in against 16.8 in. Its half-width is 10.3 in against 11.1 in. In 2025 the three are 41.2, 17.0 and 10.6 in. The interval bands are thin, visible mainly in the enlarged edge panels.

title: Decomposition waterfall
caption: The change from 2024 to 2026 in each edge and in area, split by the identity Total = 2g + Buffer + ABS. 2g is two seasons of the 2022 to 2024 trend; Buffer and ABS are the departures from that trend in 2025 and 2026 (Delta_buffer and Delta_ABS). Each of those bars starts where the one before it ends, and whiskers are 95% intervals. Plane, right of the rule, is the mechanical plate-plane component of 2025, the mid-plate contour minus the front-plate contour. It sits outside the sum, because the decomposition uses mid-plate coordinates in every season; it is what a front-plate 2025 against mid-plate 2026 comparison adds. F2b shows the drop between the two planes by pitch type. Placebo P1 failed, so the components describe departures and name no cause. Top-edge caveat (annex 8.7, D-R0-04): every top-edge interval here is read as slightly too narrow. In the synthetic recovery the top edge's 95% interval covered the truth in 91 of 100 replicates, against a bound of 93. Its null 90% interval lay within 0.10 in of zero for 44 of 50, against 47, so a top-edge equivalence reading is underpowered. Half-width shortfall (annex 8.7): its null 90% interval covered zero in 42 of 50 replicates, against a bound of 43.
alt: Four small bar charts, one each for the top edge, bottom edge, half-width and area. In area, Buffer is -23.4 sq in and ABS -33.1 sq in, for a total of -56.0 sq in, while the separate plane bar is 12.9 sq in. The top edge moves down by 0.54 in in total and the bottom edge moves up by 0.94 in; the plane bars are -0.77 in at the top and -1.11 in at the bottom.

title: Plate-plane drop by pitch type
caption: The drop in the ball's height between the front of the plate and mid-plate, dz, for 367,593 2025 called pitches by pitch type, from W3.17's plane table. Each dot is the median, the thick bar the interquartile range and the thin bar the 5th to 95th percentiles. Rows run from the smallest median drop to the largest. The four-seam (FF) drops least, median -0.71 in (IQR -0.83 to -0.58), and the curveball (CU) most, median -1.48 in (IQR -1.64 to -1.32). This is the by-pitch-type figure D-56 and CH1-A13 ask for; the per-edge plane component is F2's Plane bar and T4's plane row.
alt: A dot-and-bar chart with one row per pitch type, 12 rows. Medians run from -0.71 in for the four-seam at the top to -1.48 in for the curveball at the bottom. Every bar lies left of zero, so every pitch type drops between the two planes.

title: Umpire caterpillar
caption: Each umpire's 2025 to 2026 response relative to the league's, in inches, as a posterior median with a 90% interval from W3.18's primary model, for the 88 umpires with cells in both seasons, ranked. No umpire is named: CH1-A6's reliability gate was not met, so under D-21 no per-umpire row is published. The inset is the posterior of tau, the between-umpire SD of the response. Its rule marks CH1-A6's materiality threshold, 0.20 in, and P(tau >= 0.20 in) is 0.000.
alt: A caterpillar plot of 88 short vertical intervals, ranked from lowest to highest, centred close to zero; 0 of the 90% intervals exclude zero. An inset density of tau has a median of 0.041 in, and lies almost entirely left of the 0.20 in threshold.

title: Surface calibration by d bin
caption: In-sample calibration of the primary surface by 0.5-inch bins of d, the signed distance of the ball centre from the zone edge, over +/-8 in. Each point is the observed called-strike rate minus the mean fitted probability, in percentage points, with a 95% Wilson interval on the observed rate. 1,153,067 fitted pitches; the fitted probabilities include the umpire effects. Out-of-sample calibration is F8's, on the sealed set.
